content.explanation: A compiler converts source code into machine code. Early compilers are often written in another language. Over time, a compiler may become capable of compiling its own source code. This process is called compiler bootstrapping. Many modern programming languages use self-hosted compilers because it allows the language ecosystem to evolve independently.
content.example: Early C++ compilers were built using C before becoming self-hosted.
content.analogy: A teacher trains a student who later becomes a teacher and trains future students.
content.keyTakeaway: Compiler bootstrapping enables a compiler to eventually compile itself.
